subject: Secure build runbook + change-trace deliverables
messages:
From: Patrick Morris <patrick.morris@assessaudit.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: security_team@finbank.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: secure-build runbook + change trace for SIG

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our SIG intake for FinBank we need a compact package showing how Redwood enforces build security and documents change approvals. Specifically we're looking for: 1) a build/runbook that describes gated CI steps, signing/verification and ephemeral credential usage; 2) an export of recent change requests (tickets) tied to releases for the last 6 months; and 3) short logs showing secret rotation events (anonymized ok).

If you can provide the artifacts or point us to a secure share, that would be great — target due date: Fri 24 Sep EOD Pacific. If anything on scope needs to change, flag it here.

Best,
Patrick Morris
Senior Assessor, AssessAudit
patrick.morris@assessaudit.com

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Patrick Morris <patrick.morris@assessaudit.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: secure-build runbook + change trace for SIG

Patrick — thanks, we can deliver. Quick note on scope: the change export will include ticket metadata and approval timestamps but not full commit diffs (we provide commit SHAs and CI run links instead). Secrets logs will be redacted to hide key material; they will show rotation timestamps and actor IDs.

I've attached: redwood_secure_build_runbook_v1.3.pdf (runbook; includes gating, signing steps, and ephemeral credential flow) and an initial sample of secret-rotation-sample-logs.txt. Soojin and Marissa are copied to add CI pipeline snippets and the change-export.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Today (09/22): runbook + rotation logs (attached)
- Thu 09/23: CI snippet + exported ticket list (SUP-9345 export)
- Fri 09/24 EOD: consolidated package + signed attestation (if FinBank needs a signed letter)

If that's acceptable I'll proceed and gather the SUP export and the Jira run history.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_secure_build_runbook_v1.3.pdf; secret-rotation-sample-logs.txt

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Patrick Morris <patrick.morris@assessaudit.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: secure-build runbook + change trace for SIG

Patrick / Irene — attaching a minimal CI snippet that highlights the gated stages, artifact signing step (cosign), and references to ephemeral credential provider (ep-vault). The attached ci_pipeline_snippet.yaml is trimmed — full pipeline lives in our internal ASM but we can provide a sanitized export.

A couple clarifications for the assessor:
- Code review: all merges to main require at least two approvals and a passing static-analysis job. The runbook steps 3.2–3.6 show the gates.
- Signing: we use cosign with a hardware-protected key on build runners; the runbook lists KMS/HSM integration points.
- Change trace: SUP-9345 is the ticket export we'll attach; it includes approver ids, timestamps, and associated release tags. Commit-level provenance is supplied as SHA references only.

I'll load the CSV export into a secure Drive folder and share the link by EOD.

Sooj
Soojin Lee
Engineering Manager, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ci_pipeline_snippet.yaml

From: Patrick Morris <patrick.morris@assessaudit.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: secure-build runbook + change trace for SIG

Thanks Soojin — that snippet clarifies things. One follow-up: for the change-export we need the approval chain for three production releases in the last six months (ticket id, approver emails, timestamps, and the linked release tag). If the export can include a short provenance mapping (ticket -> release tag -> CI run ID), that will speed our review. Also confirm whether the artifact signing key lives in a customer-managed HSM or Redwood-managed key store.

Patrick

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Patrick Morris <patrick.morris@assessaudit.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2027 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: secure-build runbook + change trace for SIG

Patrick — final package attached and shared to the secure Drive link below. Contents: redwood_secure_build_runbook_v1.3.pdf, ci_pipeline_snippet.yaml, change-management-export_SUP-9345.csv (includes ticket -> release tag -> CI run ID mapping for the three releases you asked), and secret-rotation-sample-logs.txt (redacted).

To answer your question: artifact signing keys are held in a Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed key material for production signing; customers may optionally bring their own key via our Dedicated/Private offerings — the runbook explains BYOK patterns and how signing differs by deployment mode.

Drive link (secure share, view-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Crunbook-folder-id
Jira export ref: JIRA-SUP-9345
HubSpot account reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/finbank

If FinBank would like a signed attestation on letterhead, tell me the recipient name and I'll route to Legal for signature.

Thanks everyone for the quick turn.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_secure_build_runbook_v1.3.pdf; ci_pipeline_snippet.yaml; change-management-export_SUP-9345.csv; secret-rotation-sample-logs.txt
